articles.title: Actors Lee Ji-ah, Ko So-young, and Choi Myung-gil Share Recent Updates and Daily Lives via SNS
articles.summary:
Actor Lee Ji-ah shared a photo of herself sitting on a sandy beach looking out at the ocean with one knee raised. In the released photo, Lee is wearing a dark-colored sleeveless zipped vest with white shorts and large sports sunglasses. Small green and pink drawings are visible on her arm, and she is seen wearing white socks and sneakers.

Lee showed various poses, such as taking a selfie against a sky-blue structure and making a V-pose with her back to the ocean.

Actor Ko So-young shared a photo of herself wearing a beige cape over a black top and pants. The edges of the cape feature black lines and fringe details, and Ko added a sense of unity to her overall style by wearing black long boots. Her blunt bob haircut falling near her jawline, silver-colored accessories on her wrist, and small hoop earrings catch the eye.

Born in 1972, Ko is married to actor Jang Dong-gun and they have one son and one daughter. The couple resides in a penthouse located in Cheongdam-dong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, valued at approximately 16,400,000,000 won. Fans who saw the photos left comments such as, "You are so beautiful," and "Short hair suits you the best in the world."

Actor Choi Myung-gil showcased a dark-colored jacket and pants suit set against a backdrop of red brick buildings. Choi matched a light-colored top with lace details under her jacket and added focal points with multiple necklaces and rings. In a subsequent photo, she stood barefoot next an outdoor swimming pool, wearing sunglasses and smiling leisurely.

Born in 1962, Choi married novelist and politician Kim Han-gil in 1995 and they have two sons. Choi's nephew, actor Kwon Yul, married a non-celebrity on May 24 of last year. Fans left comments on Choi's photos such as, "Pretty," "So charming," and "I missed your bright smile so much."

articles.title: Singer Sim Su-bong Sparks Controversy for Publicly Criticizing Junior Kim Da-hyun on Festival Stage
articles.summary:
Singer Sim Su-bong has sparked controversy after publicly criticizing junior singer Kim Da-hyun, who performed immediately before her on stage at a festival. Sim performed on the 20th at the 10th Jinan Highland Trot Festival held in Jinan-gun, North Jeolla Province. The day's concert proceeded with Sim's performance immediately following Kim's stage.

After singing two of her hit songs, Sim grabbed the microphone and mentioned Kim, who had performed in the preceding slot. Sim stated that the young woman who sang earlier had made her head spin. She then asked if that manager was present, and declared that she seemed to be a young lady who knew nothing about what a song is or what life is.

Addressing officials backstage, Sim stated, Do not send that contestant out before me again, adding that she felt so dizzy she was about to faint. She went on to add that singing is not something one does so carelessly.

Public attention has focused on the public criticism directed at a junior singer young enough to be her granddaughter. The two are known to have crossed paths through a broadcast three years ago. Sim appeared as a special master on the MBN trot audition program Active King of Singers, which aired in December 2023.

At the time, during the one-on-one death match of the first round of the main competition, Sim chose singer Lyn, who went up against Kim. Due to Sim's choice, Kim lost and was pushed to the elimination candidate pool, but she survived through the resurrection round and finished the competition in final third place.

It remains unclear specifically which aspect of Kim's vocals or attitude Sim was pointing out. However, heavy criticism is pouring in over a veteran singer targeting a teenage junior singer on stage at a public event in front of a gathered audience.

articles.title: 'I Am Solo' Season 29 Ok-soon Shares Update from Chiang Mai Following Breakup... Eye-Catching Style
articles.summary:
Ok-soon of Season 29, who appeared on the older-woman-younger-man special of the SBS Plus and ENA dating program 'I Am Solo', recently shared photos taken in Chiang Mai via her personal Instagram account. Season 29 Ok-soon also left the caption, "This trip to Chiang Mai was even better because I was with a weaving bag that is great to carry across all four seasons ..👜🤍".

In the released photos, Season 29 Ok-soon is seen pairing a brown halter-neck top with relaxed-fit white pants. She completed her neat styling with a naturally tied hairstyle, a small necklace, and a bright-colored shoulder bag.

Season 29 Ok-soon, a nurse born in 1989, gained popularity during her time on the show and became a final couple with Season 29 Young-soo. Although they later announced through a live broadcast that they had developed into a real-life couple, the two subsequently broke up.

articles.title: ATA Festival at Sangam Nanjiji Hangang Park Concludes Successfully with Diverse Performances and Events
articles.summary:
Co-hosted by Hankung Media Group outlets including Ten Asia and Hankung.com, the 2026 Asia Top Artist Festival (hereinafter referred to as the ATA Festival), a comprehensive K-culture festival, was held for two days from September 19 to September 20 at Nanjiji Hangang Park in Sangam-dong, Seoul. Aiming to be a global cultural platform encompassing not only music performances but also K-food, K-beauty, and K-fashion, this year marked the second edition of the event.

The lineup for the first day of performances on September 19 featured Hi-Fi Unicorn, Kim Soo-young, Lee Oh-wook, Dynamic Duo, Moon Sang-min, Car the Garden, Lucy, &TEAM, Woodz, and CNBLUE. Actor Moon Sang-min showed his fandom backstage by singing a portion of Dynamic Duo's "Attendance," and shared that he usually enjoys listening to older music and rock genres, including songs by IU, Deulgukhwa, and Kim Hyun-chul.

The second day on September 20 featured performances by Dragon Pony, Choi Ye-na, Choi Hyun-wook, Daybreak, Urban Zakapa, Alpha Drive One, Lee Mu-jin, Kickflip, Jannabi, and Ateez. Choi Ye-na interacted with the audience by performing her hit songs "Catch Catch," "Nemo Nemo," and "Good Morning," while Lee Mu-jin performed "Traffic Light," "Is Anybody There?", "Tit-tit," "Episode," and "Youth Comic," followed by a surprise fan service during his final song where he threw the ATA Festival slogan towel he had been wearing on his shoulder toward the standing audience.

Outside the concert venue, interactive events, photo zones, and merchandise sales areas were operated. Various missions such as the "ATA Safe Landing Challenge," "Bias Time Catch," and "Spaceship Hammer Game" took place at the "ATA Arcade," while audiences directly decorated cheering flags at the "FLAG YOUR ARTIST" booth. In addition, surprise gifts from performing artists continued, with &TEAM distributing disposable sunglasses and CNBLUE handing out handheld fans to the audience, further heating up the festival atmosphere.

articles.title: Lim Young-woong, Ha Sung-woon, Wendy, and Kim Eui-young Take No. 1 Spots in Ten Asia Vote Categories
articles.summary:
Voting is underway on the Top Ten Ten Asia website under the theme of "singers you would want to go eat autumn gizzard shad with." The voting was divided into categories for male and female singers, as well as male and female trot singers.

Lim Young-woong took first place in the male trot singer category. To mark his 10th debut anniversary, Lim held "IM HERO - THE STADIUM 2" at the Goyang Stadium main stadium, drawing approximately 95,000 spectators. Through this concert, his cumulative concert audience since debut surpassed 1 million people, and he released the special digital album "IM HERO 10."

Ha Sung-woon claimed the No. 1 spot in the male singer category. Ha took the stage at "KCON LA 2026" held in Los Angeles, USA, where he performed a reunion stage with his Wanna One members for the first time in about 8 years.

He is also preparing to appear at the "NOL FESTIVAL" scheduled to be held at KINTEX Exhibition Center 2 in Goyang this coming October.

Red Velvet's Wendy took first place in the female singer category. Wendy made a full-group comeback after about 2 years and 2 months by releasing her new mini-album "Velvet Summer." In addition, she is continuing her steady activities as she marks the 2nd anniversary of her appointment as the DJ for SBS Power FM's "Wendy's Young Street."

Kim Eui-young placed first in the female trot singer category. Kim has been active across various stages and broadcasts, and the music tracks she released last year continue to receive steady attention.

articles.title: tvN Weekend Drama 'Four Hands' Sees Ratings Rise to 7.3%
articles.summary:
tvN weekend drama 'Four Hands' started with a 3.4% rating in its premiere, and its sixth episode broadcast on the 13th recorded 7.3%. As viewership more than doubled, the characters in the drama have grown from 17 to 27 years old, entering the second act. Previously, Kang Bi-oh (played by Song Kang), Choi Jung-yo (played by Lee Jun-young), and Hong Jae-in (played by Jang Gyu-ri) met at Korea Arts High School and grew close through music.

Kang Bi-oh helped Choi Jung-yo stand on stage as a pianist, Choi Jung-yo taught Kang Bi-oh, who was obsessed with flawless performance, how to enjoy the piano, and Hong Jae-in stayed by the two people's sides. The past sixth episode revealed the present lives of the three individuals after a span of 10 years. Kang Bi-oh has become a world-renowned pianist, Hong Jae-in joined a music management company and is working as Kang Bi-oh's manager, and Choi Jung-yo, who had vanished just before the competition finals, reappeared after 9 years as a participant in a conducting competition.

Regarding the differences between 17-year-old and 27-year-old Kang Bi-oh, Song Kang said, "Although they are the same person, I thought that as a long time has passed, the atmosphere and emotional grain would change." He added, "If 17-year-old Kang Bi-oh is a bit more sensitive and runs toward perfection, I tried to express 27-year-old Kang Bi-oh as a figure who has deepened considerably through various experiences." Lee Jun-young explained, "To show both eras—17 and 27 years old—well, I tried to make a clear difference in my acting tone and way of speaking." He continued, "I thought the most important thing was to ensure that the flow of emotions naturally accompanying the change in age does not feel awkward." Jang Gyu-ri stated, "I thought that 27-year-old Hong Jae-in would have developed various layers of emotion through diverse experiences, such as facing moments where she has to give up things she wants to do and feeling confusion in her heart toward the person she likes."

articles.title: 2nd ATA Festival Kicks Off at Nanji Hangang Park in Sangam-dong, Seoul, Featuring Dynamic Duo, Lee Oh-wook, and More
articles.summary:
The second ATA Festival, hosted by the Hankyung Media Group including Ten Asia and Hakyung.com, opened on Sept. 19 at Nanji Hangang Park in Sangam-dong, Seoul. Aiming to serve as a global cultural platform encompassing not only music performances but also K-food, K-beauty, and K-fashion, the festival features various experience booths and food and beverage zones designed for audiences to experience K-culture throughout the day.

The event runs for two days from Sept. 19 to Sept. 20.

On Sept. 19, the opening day, performers including Dynamic Duo, Lee Oh-wook, CNBLUE, LUCY, &TEAM, WOODZ, Car the Garden, Kim Soo-young, Hi-Fi Unicorn, and actor Moon Sang-min took to the stage. Among them, Lee Oh-wook kicked off the concert with "Not Afraid," heightening the energy with band sounds and guitar solos.

After finishing his performance, he remarked, "More people came than I expected, so my heart is pounding," and introduced the song by saying, "'Not Afraid' is a track I worked on with Cho Won-sang of LUCY."

Lee then added a lyrical atmosphere by passionately singing "That Winter," a song the audience could sing along with, followed by "Stop" and a cover of 2NE1's "UGLY" to heat up the mood. He also premiered his unreleased new song, "I'll Call You," scheduled for release on Oct. 30, asking for the audience's continued interest.

Closing his six-song set with Nell's "Where You Are," he traversed between intense band sounds and sweet emotions.

Dynamic Duo opened their set with "Smoke" and "AEAO." Although there was a brief sound glitch during the performance, they continued without flinching, and Gaeko drew responses from the crowd by saying, "It seems quite hot, but let's just sweat and have fun." Choiza added, "We won't do quiet songs and will keep running with more exciting ones. It's better to sweat profusely and have a great time."

Dynamic Duo subsequently performed "Confession," "Attendance Check," "Question Mark," and "See Through." Gaeko brought laughter by mentioning regarding the flame pillar stage effects, "We thought the stage effect would be a water bomb, but fire came out instead, so I felt quite apologetic while singing." Furthermore, after introducing their DJ of over 20 years as "the best scratcher in Korea," they presented a short DJing performance. Wrapping up their main set with "Wake Up" and "Friday Night," Dynamic Duo returned to the stage upon request for an encore to passionately perform "Guilty," heightening the festival's heat amid a massive sing-along.

articles.title: 'I Am Solo' Season 28 Ok-soon Shares Update from Ganghwa Visit for Father-in-Law's Birthday
articles.summary:
Ok-soon from Season 28 of "I Am Solo" recently posted photos on her Instagram along with the caption, "Last weekend, we went to Ganghwa to celebrate my father-in-law's birthday 😁🤍 We filled the weekend with delicious food and had a great time playing ㅋㅋㅋㅋ I love my family 🥰 Happy birthday to my father-in-law 🎂 Let's have a fun weekend this week too!! Have a great weekend everyone 💕."

In the released photos, Season 28 Ok-soon is standing on a wide expanse of sandy beach, smiling while making a V-sign with one hand next to her face. With her hair tied up in a high bun, she is wearing a black T-shirt and black shorts that fall above the knee, layered with a dark, oversized jacket featuring pink stripes.

She completed her casual outfit by wearing black socks that reach below her knees and light pink shoes. Behind Season 28 Ok-soon, the sandy beach and the sea stretch out widely, while an overcast sky fills most of the frame, showing an open scenery.

Born in 1991 and aged 35, Season 28 Ok-soon remarried Young-ho, who was born in 1989. Season 28 Ok-soon previously uploaded a video titled "I have a major announcement to make" on her YouTube channel "Hong Arim," where she revealed a pregnancy test and ultrasound photos alongside Season 28 Young-ho and her daughter, sharing the joyful news that she had entered a stable stage of pregnancy.

articles.title: Rhymer Unveils Daily Life at Brand New Music Headquarters, Working Alongside Father and Younger Sister
articles.summary:
Rhymer, the head of Brand New Music, has revealed his daily routine at the agency's seven-story headquarters located in Gangnam. After organizing his schedule with a planner in his executive office, Rhymer moved to the recording studio to directly direct the recording of a new song by label artist Lee Eun-sang.

Following the session, Rhymer prepared a gift for Lee Eun-sang—who now lives independently—and held a meeting with producers and staff members. After wrapping up his work, he met with his father and younger sister, who work together in the company's finance team, to have dinner.

Rhymer's father has been in charge of financial and accounting management since the company's early days, while his younger sister serves as the executive director of finance and accounting. During the meal, his father asked Rhymer if he was seeing anyone and urged him to remarry.

Rhymer talked on the phone with singer Kim Jin-pyo, expressing his romantic ideals about a cozy family. Kim Jin-pyo shared details of his daily life with his daughter and cheered on Rhymer's new beginning.

articles.title: President Lee Jae-myung Asks Special Counsel Bill to Remove Prosecution Withdrawal Authority over Fabricated Indictment Suspicions; Cho Hee-de Emphasizes Judicial Independence
articles.summary:
President Lee Jae-myung stated on the 18th during a press conference at the Blue House Guest House that the National Assembly should swiftly uncover the truth through a special counsel regarding cases suspected of being fabricated indictments. President Lee requested, "It is not desirable for unnecessary expressions to cause political battles or to spread misunderstandings about me or the government," adding, "Please delete the provisions regarding the transfer or disposition of the existing indicted cases under the controversial special counsel and focus solely on uncovering the truth." He went on to say, "I am not the only person who suffered damage from forced investigations and indictments for political purposes by the previous government," and added, "I believe it is right to uncover the truth through a special counsel regarding these malicious investigations and cases suspected of being fabrications."

Meanwhile, Chief Justice Cho Hee-de emphasized judicial independence in his closing remarks at the 20th Conference of Chief Justices of Asia and the Pacific held in Seoul on the same day. Chief Justice Cho stated, "Courts must respond to change, but the principles guiding us must remain firm," and added, "The independence, fairness, and integrity of the judiciary, as well as public trust, must always be protected." Chief Justice Cho's remarks came immediately after President Lee, during his press conference earlier that morning, fielded a question regarding the re-nomination of Supreme Court justices and remarked, "I think we need to think about why independence is granted to state institutions."

articles.title: 'Married Woman Killer' Mu Jin-sung: "Gi Yeong-do's feelings evolved from love to respect"
articles.summary:
Actor Mu Jin-sung recently shared various stories about the project and his character in an interview following the conclusion of the MBC Friday-Saturday drama 'Married Woman Killer'. Mu played the role of Gi Yeong-do, a genius hacker and assistant manager in Sales Team 3 at Durumi Electronics, serving as a dependable junior to the protagonist Yu Bo-na.

Mu explained that Gi's initial feelings toward his senior, Yu Bo-na, stemmed from romantic attraction, but gradually transformed into respect as they worked together. He also revealed that during his first shoot with co-star Gong Hyo-jin, the natural tension and excitement of meeting for the very first time were organically captured in the scene.

Mu noted that he tried to highlight comedic aspects in scenes such as his romance with Kwon Se-ah and the athletic competition, and added that Sung Dong-il, who played the team manager, helped make his character more multidimensional through improvisations and advice. Furthermore, he named Kim Tae-ri as an actor he would like to work with in the future, and expressed a strong willingness to appear in variety programs.

articles.title: Huh Young-man's Original Work 'Tazza: Beelzebub's Song' Set for Release on Oct. 23, Starring Byun Yo-han and Noh Jae-won
articles.summary:
The film 'Tazza: Beelzebub's Song' has released stills of its main characters and a Texas Hold'em introduction video ahead of its scheduled release on the 23rd. Directed by Choi Kook-hee, the new project is a crime film adapted from the final installment of cartoonist Huh Young-man's original manhwa series.

Jang Tae-young, who achieves success through an online casino business, and his close friend of the same name, Park Tae-young—who stripped him of everything—reunite in a global gambling ring for a showdown of revenge. Byun Yo-han plays Jang Tae-young, while Noh Jae-won takes on the role of Park Tae-young, stepping into his first commercial film lead role. Ayaka Miyoshi and other actors also appear, engaging in tense matches.

The released stills capture Jang Tae-young's crazed gaze, Kaneko holding a gun with a blood-stained face, and characters of different nationalities and motives exchanging glances across a hold'em table. Advance screening attendees have responded enthusiastically to the film, with comments such as, "It captures both the thrill of the game and the catharsis of payback at once," "A running time that flies by without a moment to breathe," "Even a familiar flavor tastes better when cooked this way," "A series finale that properly finishes the job," and "The long-awaited thrill of a revenge drama."

The actors personally stepped up to explain hold'em, the movie's main subject matter, so audiences can easily understand it. In a video introducing the basic rules of combining two hole cards held in the hand with five community cards dealt on the board, along with three representative hand rankings, the two actors asked audiences to watch the film with the line, "How about it, easy right?" and delivered holiday greetings saying, "Chuseok is Tazza!" From the production stage, professional poker players such as Hong Jin-ho and Radpakk participated as advisors, designing the hands shown in the movie and structuring them so viewers can intuitively grasp wins and losses.

Regarding his feelings on taking on his first commercial film lead role, Noh Jae-won stated, "It's both new and nerve-wracking, because this is just the beginning and I want to do many projects in the future." He added, "All of this is not a given, but something to be grateful for. These days, I often think that I must never take it for granted." He also shared the story of reuniting with Byun Yo-han—with whom he built a connection through the drama 'Uncle Samsik'—and revealed an anecdote about secretly mimicking even Byun's wardrobe and meal menus to immerse himself in his character.

articles.title: 'Love in the Moonlight' Quintet Reunites for 10th Anniversary Trip, Park Bo-gum Predicts Kim Yoo-jung Will Marry First
articles.summary:
Park Bo-gum, Kim Yoo-jung, Jinyoung, Chae Soo-bin, and Kwak Dong-yeon, the stars of the KBS 2TV variety program "Love in the Moonlight," went on a 1-night, 2-day trip to Hongcheon, Gangwon Province, to celebrate their 10th debut anniversary. Reuniting to mark the 10th anniversary since the drama's conclusion, they enjoyed water activities, ate baeksuk (stewed chicken), and caught up on each other's recent lives.

While visiting a restaurant on the way, Park Bo-gum asked, "Did you get asked in interviews who would be the first to get married?" Park answered that he had picked Kim Yoo-jung as No. 1, causing Kim to look flustered as she asked, "I'm the youngest, so why did you pick me?" Park explained, "I felt like Yoo-jung would meet a good person and go off [to marry] well."

During the trip, the members gave each other nicknames and engaged in a round of friendly exposures. Park Bo-gum received the nickname "Student Council President," Kim Yoo-jung "Dr. Oh Eun-young," Chae Soo-bin "Herbivore with a Temper," Kwak Dong-yeon "Youngest Uncle," and Jinyoung "Good Hit Sensitivity." Explaining Kim Yoo-jung, Jinyoung said, "Yoo-jung is the youngest, but she's someone who can scold the older brothers," adding, "Even though she's the youngest, she has the most presence."

While discussing Jinyoung's weight, Park Bo-gum's weight also became a topic of conversation. Park revealed that his weight was 65kg during the filming of "Love in the Moonlight" and shared that his current weight is 76kg. Jinyoung's weight was known to be 66kg.

articles.title: Cheong Wa Dae Lean Toward Appointing Kim Ji-yong as Chief of Major Crime Investigation Agency Despite Ruling Party Pushback Ahead of Oct. 2 Launch
articles.summary:
President Lee Jae-myung is reported to be leaning toward appointing Kim Ji-yong as candidate for chief of the Major Crime Investigation Agency, despite opposition from prosecution reform advocates within the ruling party, it was learned on the 17th. Cheong Wa Dae plans to submit a request for a National Assembly confirmation hearing for candidate Kim soon.

Regarding the directive for additional verification of candidate Kim, a ruling party official stated that it was not a matter of his tenure status but rather a measure to re-examine the facts raised by the ruling party, adding that most of the allegations raised are viewed as inconsistent with the facts.

Vice Minister of the Interior and Safety and head of the Investigation Agency Opening Preparation Team Kim Min-jae explained that regarding the emergency travel ban case of former Vice Minister of Justice Kim Hak-ui and the official misconduct violence case involving prosecutor Jung Jin-woong—both cases in which candidate Kim was in the command line during his tenure at the prosecution—he had expressed opinions opposing indictment and was not the final decision-maker.

The Ministry of the Interior and Safety also disclosed that candidate Kim ordered a reinvestigation after deeming the existing non-indictment disposition unjust in a case involving relatives of former Prosecutor General Yoon Seok-youl. In addition, regarding candidate Kim's past record on the abolition of prosecution investigative powers, the ministry explained that it stemmed from concerns that a vacuum could occur if sufficient measures were not put in place to protect the rights of the socially vulnerable and crime victims.

Behind Cheong Wa Dae's direction toward appointing candidate Kim was the practical reality that it is difficult to delay personnel selections given the upcoming launch of the Investigation Agency on October 2. Candidate Kim is one of four individuals recommended by the Investigation Agency Candidate Recommendation Committee, and underwent the appointment recommendation procedure by Minister of the Interior and Safety Yoon Ho-jung on the 7th.

Within the ruling party, pushback over candidate Kim's selection has continued. Democratic Party lawmaker Yoon Kun-young stated on a radio broadcast that day that he is personally negative about it and doubts whether he is a person with sound views on prosecution reform.

Democratic Party lawmaker Kim Yong-min also held a press conference urging an immediate halt to the seven reactionary moves neutralizing prosecution reform and the withdrawal of Kim Ji-yong's nomination, requesting a decisive decision from the President. Gyeonggi Governor Choo Mi-ae expressed opposition the previous day by comparing candidate Kim to Nazi war criminal Adolf Eichmann.

On the other hand, Democratic Party lawmaker Kim Young-jin countered that the prosecution has been reformed to hold only indictment powers, and that it fits the establishment purpose of the Investigation Agency for a person skilled at investigations to head it.

articles.title: Kim Min-seok Proposes 15-Seat Floor Negotiation Standard, Escalating Ruling Bloc Tensions After Renewing Choo Mi-ae Criticism
articles.summary:
Democratic Party Representative Kim Min-seok proposed lowering the parliamentary floor negotiation group formation requirement from the current 20 seats to 15 seats. The Rebuilding Korea Party, which holds 12 seats, immediately pushed back and called for a normalization to 10 seats.

Appearing on "Democratic Party TV," Representative Kim stated that an alliance of progressive forces must be realized, mentioning that around 15 seats is realistic and acceptable for an initial step. He added that the 22nd National Assembly features 12 seats for the Rebuilding Korea Party, 4 seats for the Progressive Party, and 1 seat each for the Basic Income Party and the Social Democratic Party, noting that combining them is enough to form a negotiation group.

In an official statement, the Rebuilding Korea Party criticized the current 20-seat requirement as a remnant of the Yushin regime created by the Park Chung-hee administration to raise the barrier for negotiation groups. It stated that returning to the pre-Yushin standard of 10 seats is common sense and the natural course, adding that it has had no official or unofficial contact with the Democratic Party leadership regarding an alliance.

Chung Chun-sang, secretary-general of the Rebuilding Korea Party, also argued via Facebook that lowering the negotiation group requirement from 20 seats to 15 seats would have no reform effect. An lawmaker from the Rebuilding Korea Party expressed displeasure, stating that the 15-seat policy means the party will not be allowed to form a negotiation group on its own.

Alongside this, Representative Kim presented political reform tasks, including improving the single-member district system and the semi-linked proportional representation system, introducing a presidential runoff voting system, and devising competitive single-candidate unification methods. Ahead of last year's presidential election, the Democratic Party and four opposition parties issued a joint declaration announcing plans to pursue relaxing negotiation group requirements and introducing a runoff voting system immediately after the presidential election.

Meanwhile, tensions within the ruling bloc continue over Gyeonggi Governor Choo Mi-ae's criticism of President Lee Jae-myung's prosecution reform. Representative Kim compared Governor Choo's remarks to the precursor situation during the impeachment of former President Roh Moo-hyun, warning against internal division.

At the first joint meeting of provincial and municipal party committee chairpersons held at the party headquarters, Representative Kim mentioned the inspection vacuum for local government heads and emphasized the need to protect the party's platform and dignity. While interpretations emerged that this targeted Governor Choo, the Rebuilding Korea Party pushed back, calling it "sycophant politics" that tries to silence bitter criticism. Within the party, lawmakers including Park Jie-won urged restraint, stating that both Governor Choo and Representative Kim were going too far.

articles.title: China Formalizes AI Loss-of-Control Risks and Dual-Regulation Pressures on South Korean Firms
articles.summary:
Reuters reported that Chinese authorities are undertaking legal and technical preparations for scenarios involving the loss of control over artificial intelligence, citing safety frameworks and the latest guidelines from the Cyberspace Administration of China. As regulations on autonomous agents take concrete shape, analysts suggest that South Korean AI developers seeking to enter the Chinese market could face a dual-regulation burden, requiring them to additionally develop mandatory intervention modules tailored to local specifications.

Through an artificial intelligence safety framework released in September 2024, the Cyberspace Administration of China officially specified the possibility that future artificial intelligence might autonomously secure external resources, self-replicate, form a sense of self, and compete with humans for control. The administration subsequently issued a revised edition of the framework in September of last year, further detailing risk scenarios. The revised proposal specifies that artificial intelligence could achieve a sudden leap in intelligence beyond unexpected levels before securing resources, engaging in self-replication, and pursuing power.

Consequently, new governance principles focused on trust-based utilization and the prevention of control loss were added. Expert commentaries published on state-run websites later explained that these principles are intended to protect human survival and development from the runaway risks of artificial intelligence.

Chinese President Xi Jinping attended the World Artificial Intelligence Conference held in Shanghai last July and urged attention to both the inherent and derivative risks of artificial intelligence. He emphasized that artificial intelligence must always remain under human control.

Related remarks continued on the international stage. Sun Xiaobo, senior official for artificial intelligence at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated at a United Nations meeting last month that China is accelerating research on comprehensive artificial intelligence legislation. Sun Lei, China's deputy permanent representative to the United Nations, urged caution in the military use of artificial intelligence during the September meeting to prevent arms races and strategic miscalculations.

As Chinese authorities mandated developers to incorporate intervention and blocking tools and guarantee ultimate user decision-making rights through agent-specific guidelines last May, South Korean artificial intelligence service developers collaborating with local companies now inevitably face the development of additional security modules matching these specifications. The North American-style open guardrail system refers to an open-source-based artificial intelligence safety and security control framework centered around the artificial intelligence technology ecosystem in North America, including the United States. The most significant difference between the two systems lies in the degree of state intervention.

The risk of dual regulation could be alleviated if a unified artificial intelligence safety standard is reached under United Nations leadership. The direction of global standard-setting by international organizations such as the United Nations, alongside the timing for the South Korean Ministry of Science and ICT to overhaul subordinate statutes under the Artificial Intelligence Basic Act, remain key points to watch.

articles.title: Export-Import Bank of Korea Pursues $70M On-Lending Facility with Kazakhstan's ForteBank
articles.summary:
The Export-Import Bank of Korea has agreed to pursue a $70 million on-lending facility with ForteBank, a major private commercial bank in Kazakhstan. This agreement is designed to support South Korean companies entering the Kazakh market, focusing on five consumer goods sectors: food, beauty and cosmetics, power and renewable energy, machinery and equipment, and information and communication technology.

On-lending is an indirect financing method in which the Export-Import Bank of Korea lends funds to a local overseas bank, which in turn loans the money to local companies importing South Korean products. This agreement marks the first on-lending limit established with a local private bank since the Export-Import Bank of Korea resumed its on-lending program in Kazakhstan last year, 10 years after it was halted.

Additionally, the Export-Import Bank of Korea signed a memorandum of understanding with the Ministry of Energy of Kazakhstan to implement the Economic Innovation Partnership Program. Through this initiative, the bank plans to provide customized policy consulting for Kazakhstan's eco-friendly energy transition projects.

articles.title: President Lee Jae-myung to Hold Press Conference on Dec. 18 Amid Slumping Approval Ratings; Focus Expected on Consecutive-Term Constitutional Amendment and Dropping of Indictments
articles.summary:
President Lee Jae-myung will hold his seventh press conference since taking office on the 18th to directly state his positions on key state affairs. The conference will last for 90 minutes, featuring an opening statement by the president, a question-and-answer session with reporters, and closing remarks. Divided into politics-diplomacy and policy-economy sessions, the event is scheduled to take place with approximately 150 domestic and foreign reporters in attendance.

This press conference has been arranged at a time when President Lee's approval ratings for state affairs have recently been on a downward trend. According to a survey of 2515 voters nationwide conducted by Realmeter at the request of Energy Economy Newspaper from the 7th to the 11th, President Lee's positive evaluation dropped 3.8% points from the previous week to 33.8%. The negative evaluation rose 3.8% points to record 63.3%, surpassing the 60% threshold for the first time since taking office, while a Gallup Korea poll also showed a record low positive evaluation of 38%.

In the party approval rating survey, the People Power Party recorded 42.1% and the Democratic Party of Korea recorded 36.1%, showing a reversal in support between the two major parties.

The presidential office stated that this conference will deliver clear messages on issues that have sparked ongoing controversy, such as a constitutional amendment allowing consecutive terms, the dropping of indictments, and the deployment of troops to the Strait of Hormuz. In particular, both inside and outside the ruling bloc, points have been raised that the administration must respond head-on to the controversies surrounding the consecutive-term constitutional amendment and the dropping of indictments.

Additionally, remarks are expected regarding recent personnel controversies involving lawmaker Yong Hye-in, who fell through as a nominee for Minister of Gender Equality and Family, and Minister of Justice nominee Kim Seung-won, who has faced allegations of lobbying the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.

Meanwhile, the Board of Audit and Inspection announced that the presidential office under the Yoon Suk-yeol administration intervened in the decision-making process to sell the entire stake, known as a "bulk sale," during the sale of YTN in 2023. According to the audit results by the Board of Audit and Inspection, then-Senior Presidential Secretary for State Affairs Planning Lee Kwan-seop conveyed to then-Vice Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy Kang Sung-jin that the sale of the entire stake was the firm stance of the Korea Communications Commission, thereby infringing upon the autonomy of public institutions in decision-making. The Board of Audit and Inspection sent investigative reference materials regarding then-Korea Communications Commission Chairman Lee Dong-gwan and former Vice Minister Kang to the Corruption Investigation Office for High-Ranking Officials.

articles.title: Movie 'Tazza: Beelzebub's Song' Opens on 23rd to Conclude the Series
articles.summary:
The movie "Tazza: Beelzebub's Song," the final installment of the crime entertainment film series that began in 2006, is scheduled to open on the coming 23rd. This new work severs connections to the worldviews of the preceding three films and is structured as an independent story.

The film depicts a high-stakes, life-or-death showdown on the global hold 'em scene, entangled in betrayal and revenge between Jang Tae-young, who achieved success through an online casino business, and his close friend Park Tae-young, who stripped him of everything. Based on the fourth part of the webtoon of the same name by authors Huh Young-man and Kim Se-young, the film expands its stage to South Korea, Japan, and Vietnam.

Byun Yo-han, who plays the lead role, lost more than 10kg to portray the emaciated appearance of Jang Tae-young, who narrowly cheats death in Vietnam. During this process, he even visited the emergency room due to hypoglycemia shock.

Director Choi Kook-hee included numerous homages to the first "Tazza" film released in 2006 throughout this work. Alongside dialogue reminiscent of "Asura Balbalta," he placed elements such as the camera angle of Kim Hye-soo's bed scene from the first film and Kwak Chul-yong's tie pin across various parts of the movie.

articles.title: Democratic Party Leader Kim Min-seok Compares Gyeonggi Governor Choo Mi-ae's Criticism of President Lee Jae-myung to Precursors of Roh Moo-hyun Impeachment
articles.summary:
Democratic Party Leader Kim Min-seok has pointed out that the internal party currents of criticism directed at President Lee Jae-myung are similar to the atmosphere during the impeachment of former President Roh Moo-hyun. Appearing on the Democratic Party's official YouTube channel "Minjoo Party TV" on the 14th, Kim made the remarks while criticizing the internal criticisms taking place at a time when the party must gather its strength as one. Previously, Gyeonggi Governor Choo Mi-ae criticized on the 12th that the President is riding on the backs of insurrection forces and walking on eggshells, regarding the nomination of lawyer Kim Ji-yong, a former prosecutor, as the inaugural chief of the Serious Crime Investigation Agency.

Kim directly targeted these remarks, stating that it is difficult to think of them as coming from a governor of his own party, and demanded an explanation from Governor Choo as to why she made such statements. Subsequently, at the 1st joint meeting of provincial and city party chapter chairmen held at the party headquarters on the 15th, he mentioned that there are many oversight gaps in the operational scope of local government heads. Kim added that leaving local government heads as they are—who act nice to the party and party members only until they receive their nominations and then turn into monarchs—is not right for local autonomy and democracy.

The Rebuilding Korea Party criticized Kim's remarks, calling it an attitude of turning reality on its head by trying to shut down harsh truths and dismissing even legitimate loyal advice as "friendly fire." In a commentary, Rebuilding Korea Party Spokesperson Im Myeong-hee pushed back, stating that such behavior is a classic example of flattering politics that blinds and deafens the President, cutting off communication with public sentiment. Voices of concern were also raised within the party regarding the standoff between the two sides.

Democratic Party Lawmaker Park Jie-won appeared on a radio broadcast and pointed out that both Governor Choo and Leader Kim were going too far.

articles.title: Director Choi Kook-hee: Homages to Kim Hye-soo's Bed Scene Angle and Kwak Chul-yong's Tie Pin—'Even Those Born in 2006 Should Watch the Previous Films' ('Tazza 4') [TEN Interview]
articles.summary:
Excitement and tension crossed the face of director Choi Kook-hee, who took the helm for the finale of "Tazza," a crime-entertainment franchise beloved for 20 years. Opening with the remark, "I'm curious about the audience's reaction and nervous," he candidly discussed the intense agony and hidden behind-the-scenes stories leading up to compressing the massive original work into 129 minutes. On the 15th, at a cafe in Samcheong-dong, Seoul, TEN Asia met with director Choi Kook-hee, who directed the film "Tazza: Beelzebub's Song" (hereinafter "Tazza 4").

Opening on the 23rd, "Tazza 4" is a film adaptation of the original cartoon by authors Huh Young-man and Kim Se-young, depicting a high-stakes, life-or-death battle of betrayal and revenge woven between Jang Tae-young (played by Byun Yo-han), who achieved success with an online casino business, and his close friend Park Tae-young (played by Noh Jae-won), who stripped him of everything. The board has expanded from traditional hwatu parlors to global hold'em. Director Choi stated, "I enjoyed the previous works so much that I wanted to make this final installment even better and show it to the audience." Adapting the massive original work spanning 10 volumes was "the process of extracting the essence." Director Choi introduced it, saying, "I focused on the emotions of jealousy, envy, and betrayal between Jang Tae-young and Park Tae-young.

It is a work that delves deeper into the emotional sentiment and drama of the characters compared to the previous installments."

The casting also prioritized bringing out the feel of the cartoon. Director Choi recalled, "When imagining actors resembling the art style of the original, Byun Yo-han was the first choice, and Noh Jae-won also fit the original's Park Tae-young." To capture the haggardness and desperation of Jang Tae-young, who returned from the brink of death in Vietnam, Director Choi asked Byun Yo-han to lose weight. Byun lost more than 10kg, and during the diet, he even visited the emergency room due to hypoglycemia shock.

Director Choi said, "Even though actor Byun Yo-han is someone who really loves alcohol, he cut out even drinking and strictly followed (the diet routine). I was truly grateful."

Rapper Swings is making his film debut as actor Moon Ji-hoon through this project. Director Choi shared, "He recently sent 300,000 won worth of Korean beef as a gift for my birthday. He looks tough, but he's truly human," and added, "Despite it being his first acting challenge, he was so full of passion that the on-site staff went out of their way to help him."

Trying to capture the brilliant performances of many actors in a single film resulted in an initial rough cut running a staggering four and a half hours. Having reduced the final running time to 129 minutes, Director Choi confessed, "We designed the games one by one with professional poker players. The actors even memorized the betting, which is no small task.

However, from the audience's perspective, they were repetitive scenes, so we had no choice but to cut them out, which is regrettable." Notably, the footage of former pro-gamer and professional poker player Hong Jin-ho, who participated as an advisor and cameo, was cut entirely. Director Choi burst into laughter and said, "Hong Jin-ho's footage was the first one I deleted. Looking at the film as a whole, it was honestly an unnecessary scene.

When I delivered the news over the phone, he said, 'I figured as much.'" He then explained, "To show Park Tae-young's jealousy and Jang Tae-young's thirst for revenge within a short time, we had no choice but to cut half of it."

Director Choi infused his sentiment of tribute toward the previous works with scenes paying homage to "Tazza 1." From lines reminiscent of "Asura Balbalta," Noh Jae-won's tie pin reminiscent of the character "Kwak Chul-yong," to Ayaka Miyoshi's bed scene angle looking back from the bed, it is close to a spin-off in terms of content, but he embedded directorial links to the first film. Director Choi smiled as he said, "It's both praise for the first film and gives fans who enjoyed the first film some fun in spotting them. There are quite a few hidden homages, and I'm curious if the audience will be able to find all of them."

He also shared behind-the-scenes stories about meeting original author Huh Young-man. Having shared a meal, Director Choi said, "The teacher showed his affection by saying, 'Among the originals, I think part 4 is the most cinematic, and though it was made too late, I am truly grateful that it was made even now,'" adding, "I think he felt it was the most cinematic because it has clear good and evil and is a thorough revenge drama." However, expressing regret that author Huh, who has recently been hospitalized for deteriorating health, has not yet been able to see the film, he cheered him on, saying, "I believe he will recover soon and definitely watch the completed film in the theater."

"Tazza," which began in 2006, is drawing its grand conclusion in 2026 after 20 years of time.

articles.title: Pro-Ruling Bloc Infighting Escalates Into Emotional Feud as Kim Min-seok Reacts to Choo Mi-ae's Criticism and Cho Kuk Joins In
articles.summary:
A war of words within the broader ruling bloc regarding the causes behind the weakening momentum of state affairs is intensifying. The internal friction, which originated from debates over the direction of prosecution reform, is descending into an emotional feud marked by harsh expressions such as "collaboration with insurrection forces," "precursor to impeachment," and "sycophant politics." Amid growing concerns that reform and policy debates have disappeared as approval ratings decline, criticism emerged within the Democratic Party on May 15 that Representative Kim Min-seok needs to exercise political leadership rather than make impulsive responses.

The conflict within the ruling camp that failed to be patched up even after the national convention has been on a steady escalation path since Gyeonggi Governor Choo Mi-ae criticized President Lee Jae-myung on May 12. The war of words appears to be heightening in intensity as Representative Kim criticized Governor Choo, and the Rebuilding Korea Party joined the fray to issue a counter-rebuttal. On May 12, regarding the nomination of lawyer Kim Ji-yong, a former prosecutor, as the head of the Major Crime Investigation Agency, Governor Choo stated, "The president is leaning on insurrection forces and walking on eggshells." On May 14, Representative Kim criticized Governor Choo on the Democratic Party's YouTube channel "Democratic Party TV," saying, "It is a situation similar to the prelude to the period when forces inside and outside the party joined hands to try to impeach President Roh Moo-hyun."

In response, the head of the Innovation Policy Research Institute of the Rebuilding Korea Party, Cho Kuk, stated, "If it goes like this, the notion of 'impeachment of Lee Jae-myung' gets disseminated. Don't they know 'Don't Think of an Elephant'?" That same day on "Democratic Party TV," Representative Kim said, "It is regime-shaking disguised as worry." At the first joint meeting of city and provincial party committee chairpersons held at the party headquarters, Representative Kim also remarked, "The activity spheres of local governments, especially local government heads, often represent an inspection blind spot." He added, "Leaving alone local government heads who act nice to the party and party members only until they receive nomination and then become kings once it is over is not right in view of local autonomy and democracy"—remarks that could be interpreted as targeting Governor Choo.

Rebuilding Korea Party Spokesperson Lim Myung-hee released a commentary stating, "(Representative Kim's criticism of Governor Choo is) petty target-setting." The spokesperson added, "The shameless attitude of blocking bitter advice and dismissing even legitimate loyal counsel as friendly fire—that is the very textbook sycophant politics that blinds and deafens the president and blocks communication with public sentiment." As warning lights flash for the administration and the ruling party due to the continuous decline in approval ratings for President Lee and the ruling party, criticism is rising that the leadership of the broader ruling bloc is merely engaging in emotional arguments that employ harsh expressions to pass the buck to opponents. In particular, opinions are being raised that rather than standing at the center of the verbal dispute, Representative Kim should exercise his political influence in a direction that heals the conflicts.

Democratic Party lawmaker Park Ji-won said on a CBS radio broadcast, "I understand Representative Kim's loyal heart, but the leader of the ruling party should embrace and refine issues rather than cause them, helping the president succeed. Both Governor Choo and Representative Kim are going too far." Regarding Representative Kim's impeachment remark, a Democratic Party lawmaker said, "It is unnecessary talk. There was no need to bring up such talk at this time, and it is amplifying (the controversy)." The lawmaker continued, "Representative Kim is reacting too sensitively to hardliners like Governor Choo.

Shouldn't we embrace everyone and move forward even if it is difficult?"

Another Democratic Party lawmaker pointed out, "Given that other lawmakers are also criticizing Governor Choo's remarks, it is desirable for the party leader to show an encompassing demeanor rather than directly refuting them yourself." The lawmaker added, "I am worried that discussions on truly important real estate or livelihood policies are being overshadowed."

articles.title: U.S. AI Firms Urge Slowdown After Securing Market Lead, Leaving South Korea Scrambling
articles.summary:
Experts generally agree with the rationale behind calls to adjust the pace of artificial intelligence development, but express concern that it could become a barrier to entry for South Korea as it chases the U.S.-China duopoly. They warn it could amount to the leading group "pulling up the ladder." Kang Jung-soo, a research center head at Bluedot AI, said in a phone interview on the 15th, "A series of events are occurring that demonstrate how AI can unintentionally cause harm to others. This is not just an issue for Anthropic or OpenAI, but a warning example for South Korean companies as well, which could affect their competitiveness." The problem is who sets the AI safety standards.

Because U.S. companies have already preempted the AI market, stricter standards built around them could act as a market entry barrier for latecomers like South Korea. Lee Seung-hyun, an adjunct professor in the Department of Global Culture and Trade at Hanyang University ERICA, said, "Of course, stability and reliability must be considered, but if we are not careful, it could become 'pulling up the ladder' and prevent us from narrowing the gap.

U.S. companies want to lead global standards, which means all AI could end up centered around the United States." Professor Lee added, "South Korea must also participate in global discussions. It is undesirable for the U.S.

and China to collude in setting standards, so in-depth discussions are needed on what stance South Korea should take."

Some point out a discrepancy between the words and actions of U.S. AI companies. Lee Hong-lak, co-director of research at LG AI Research, also said at a talk concert event on the 14th, "If anything, (U.S.

companies) are accelerating computing power and research and development (R&D) rather than decelerating, and I understand this as simply needing a bit more cautious review before launching models."

AI safety and cybersecurity are also tied to "AI sovereignty." Back in June, Anthropic formed the security coalition "Project Glasswing" and made its latest Mythos model available exclusively to member organizations, while the U.S. government previously classified AI security issues as a national security matter and imposed export controls on Mythos. At the time, South Korea inevitably took a hit from the export controls.

South Korea is only at the beginning stages, having recently seen the government designate the Naver Cloud consortium as the executing organization for developing a cybersecurity-focused AI foundation model. Consequently, opinions suggest that beyond simply using AI, the country must build the national capability to independently assess risks, and to halt and recover when necessary. Focusing on AI safety and cybersecurity could also become a new competitive edge.

Lee Won-tae, a distinguished professor at Kookmin University and chairman of the Security Special Committee under the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy Committee, said, "Moving beyond the dichotomy of 'development versus regulation,' the government must rapidly secure domestic frontier AI capabilities while securing AI sovereignty to independently test, verify, and control them." He continued, "Safety, security, and resilience must be reflected in the design and evaluation of independent AI foundation models, and in the short term, we must build dedicated security harnesses and a national AI red team system to safely select and replace multiple domestic and international models."
